sources.entry: SquirrelDisk - Open-source disk usage analyzer with sunburst and treemap views for disks and cloud storage. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/adileo/squirreldisk) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
SquirrelDisk - Disk usage analyzer with animated sunburst and treemap views that can also scan SSH servers and cloud storage via rclone.

summary.one_liner: SquirrelDisk is a free, open-source disk usage analyzer for macOS, Windows and Linux that visualizes folder sizes as a sunburst or treemap and helps you clean them up.
summary.what_it_does: It scans a disk and draws every folder as a slice of a sunburst (or a box in a treemap), sized by the space it uses, with the chart building live during the scan. Clicking a slice zooms in, hovering shows the contents, and small files are grouped so the chart stays readable. Items can be collected and moved to the Trash, deleted permanently (optionally with a three-pass DoD 5220.22-M overwrite), or copied to an external drive or cloud. It reports real on-disk size, counts cloud-only files as zero, and can scan SSH servers and cloud storage through rclone. It also offers a folder context-menu entry and a "squirreldisk scan" terminal command that prints the biggest items as a tree or JSON. The README describes it as a Rust rewrite (SquirrelDisk 2) that is actively maintained.
use_cases: find what is using up disk space
visualize folder sizes on a disk
scan a remote server over SSH for disk usage
check cloud storage usage through rclone
securely erase files before deleting them
how_to_run: Download the macOS .dmg, Windows .msi/.exe or Linux AppImage/.tar.gz from the releases page
Build from source: install Rust, then run: cargo run --release
On Linux, build dependencies: libasound2-dev libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev (Debian/Ubuntu)
notable: Sunburst and treemap views that build live during the scan
Scans SSH servers and cloud storage (S3, Google Drive, Dropbox, FTP and more) via rclone
Terminal command: squirreldisk scan with tree or JSON output
Portable mode using a 'portable' folder next to the executable
caveats: macOS requires manual approval (Open Anyway or xattr command) since the app is distributed outside the App Store
Windows shows a protection warning on first run that must be bypassed manually
Linux builds need extra development packages to compile from source
